long_biography.plain_text:
An investor in healthcare innovation before becoming a biotechnology founder, Wendy Commins Holman spent fifteen years at Ziff Brothers Investments and its public-equities arm. She led healthcare research and developed a focus on technologies that could change treatment for serious disease. She later co-founded Ridgeback Biotherapeutics with Wayne Holman and took charge of its day-to-day leadership.

At Ridgeback, Holman backed programmes against emerging infectious diseases. The company advanced an Ebola antibody therapy through US approval and partnered with Merck to develop the antiviral molnupiravir. Beyond the business, she serves as a University of Pennsylvania trustee and supports biomedical research and education there. Her work brings together investment judgement, clinical development and an interest in improving access to treatment.
